Rebuilding an Online Reputation in 90 Days: A Phase-by-Phase Plan

By RMA — Web Reputation Agency

Ninety days is enough to rebuild an online reputation on solid foundations: a complete audit, every justified removal and delisting request submitted, new owned assets live, a steady flow of genuine reviews and a monitoring routine in place. It is usually not enough to see every ranking change or every decision from Google, platforms or the Italian authorities, so the plan below measures progress phase by phase rather than promising a clean page one on day ninety.

What a 90-day plan can realistically deliver

The first three months decide the direction of the whole recovery. In this period you can establish the facts, act on everything that can be removed, start building what should replace it and change the customer signals that platforms show. Results that depend on third parties, such as a reconsidered deindexing request, a complaint to the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali or a court order in Italy, follow their own timetables and often extend beyond the window.

The phases overlap deliberately, because waiting for removals before creating content wastes weeks. The table summarises the schedule and the metric that shows whether each phase is on track.

PhaseDaysKey metric
Audit and priorities1–15Every negative item classified with an assigned tool
Removals and legal requests10–45Requests submitted and decisions received
New assets and owned content30–75New pages indexed and ranking for branded queries
Reviews and customer signals45–90Monthly volume of genuine reviews and average rating
Monitoring and next cycle80–90 and beyondShare of page one that is positive or neutral

Days 1–15: audit and priorities

Recovery begins with a precise inventory of what people see, because effort spent on low-visibility items is effort taken away from the results that actually cost you customers. Search your brand and the names of key people from an Italian location on desktop and mobile, and record everything that appears on the first two pages, together with reviews, autocomplete suggestions and AI-generated answers.

  • Classify each negative item: false or defamatory, outdated, privacy-related, a policy violation, or legitimate criticism.
  • Assign the tool for each: removal at source, delisting, legal action, public reply or suppression through new content.
  • Rank items by visibility and harm, starting with whatever appears in the top five results or on the Business Profile.
  • Preserve certified evidence of anything that may lead to legal action before you contact anyone.
  • Record baseline metrics so that progress can be measured objectively at day ninety.

At this stage also fix the cause if it still exists. Restoring a reputation while the service problem that created it continues only produces new complaints.

Days 10–45: removals and legal requests

Submit every justified request in this window, in order of priority, because platform and Google decisions take time and the clock should start as early as possible. Requests with a weak basis should be dropped rather than sent, since rejected requests can make later attempts harder.

Typical actions include policy reports for reviews that break platform rules, as described in our guide on removing negative Google reviews; notices to hosts under the Digital Services Act for illegal content; erasure requests to site owners under article 17 GDPR; right-to-be-forgotten requests to Google for outdated personal information; and, where the facts justify it, a lawyer's letter or a defamation complaint within the three-month deadline. Choosing between deletion, delisting and suppression is explained in our comparison of the three approaches. Track each request in a log with date, channel, reference number and outcome.

Days 30–75: new assets and owned content

To restore online reputation in search, you need credible pages that deserve to rank for your name, not simply the absence of negative ones. Delisted results leave gaps that Google fills with whatever is available, and that should be content you control or that presents you fairly.

Start with the assets that rank fastest for branded queries: a strengthened official website with separate pages for company information, team, services and press; complete profiles on LinkedIn and other relevant networks; an optimised Google Business Profile; and listings in Italian professional registers and trade directories. Then add earned content such as interviews in sector media, conference pages and partner case studies. Publish steadily rather than all at once, since a sudden burst of thin pages looks artificial and rarely holds its positions.

Days 45–90: reviews and customer signals

Online reputation repair is incomplete while the review profile still tells the old story. A consistent flow of recent, genuine reviews dilutes old negative ones and shows that the situation has changed, provided it is built within platform rules.

A compliant routine usually involves the following:

  1. asking every customer for feedback at a natural moment, such as delivery or the end of a service;
  2. using the same request for everyone, without filtering satisfied customers or offering incentives;
  3. replying to every new review, positive or negative, within a few days;
  4. passing recurring complaints back to operations so that they stop appearing.

Our article on collecting reviews without breaking platform rules details the method. Any purchased or invented review undoes the work, since platforms can remove reviews in bulk and the Italian Consumer Code treats fake reviews as an unfair commercial practice.

Day 90 and beyond: monitoring and the next cycle

At day ninety, compare every metric with the baseline and decide what the second cycle should focus on. Typically some requests are still pending, new assets are climbing but not yet on page one, and the review rating has started to move.

A reputation is rebuilt by sequence and consistency: remove what is unlawful, outrank what is outdated and outnumber what is unfair.

Keep a weekly monitoring routine for brand mentions, reviews and branded search, and a monthly review of the request log. Pending cases may need escalation, for example a complaint to the Garante after a Google refusal. Companies and professionals in Italy often see the most visible improvement between the fourth and the sixth month, once new assets settle into stable positions.
